input:
The vector equation of the line 2x + 4 = 3y + 1 = 6z - 3 is

Options:
A. r̄ = (2î + (1/3)ĵ + (1/2)k̂) + λ(3î + 2ĵ + k̂)
B. r̄ = (-2î - (1/3)ĵ + (1/2)k̂) + λ(3î + 2ĵ + k̂)
C. r̄ = (2î + ĵ + k̂) + λ(3î + 2ĵ + k̂)
D. r̄ = (-2î - ĵ + k̂) + λ(3î + 2ĵ + k̂)

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Convert the given Cartesian equation of line 2x + 4 = 3y + 1 = 6z - 3 into vector form r̄ = ā + λb̄.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Convert to standard Cartesian form (x - x₀)/a = (y - y₀)/b = (z - z₀)/c by dividing by coefficients of x, y, z.

key_concepts: Standard Cartesian form of line: (x - x₀)/a = (y - y₀)/b = (z - z₀)/c
Vector form of line: r̄ = ā + λb̄ where ā = (x₀, y₀, z₀) and b̄ = (a, b, c)

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Factor out coefficients of x, y, z, divide through by LCM(2,3,6) = 6 to get standard Cartesian form, extract point ā and direction b̄, and write in vector form.
logical_steps: Step 5: Vector equation r̄ = (-2î - (1/3)ĵ + (1/2)k̂) + λ(3î + 2ĵ + k̂)

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: Line passes through (-2, -1/3, 1/2) with direction ratios (3, 2, 1). Checks out: 2(-2)+4 = 0, 3(-1/3)+1 = 0, 6(1/2)-3 = 0 ✓
